summary: Masahiro Inami specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University (~1984–1989) and held a teaching post at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1993).

Masahiro Kusunoki worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1947–1953), where he later served as chair professor of religious studies and history of religion (~1967–1980).

Masahiro Shimoda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1982–1994), he served as professor there (2001–2002) and held visiting appointments at SOAS (2006), Stanford (2010), and the University of Virginia (2012).
Masahiro Takano is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and served as a librarian there.

Masakazu Tanaka specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1980) and earned his Ph.D. at the London School of Economics and Political Science (~1981–1986), later holding a post at Kyoto University (1988–2019).
Masaki Ichinose is a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1977–1988). He held an academic post at the University of Tokyo (~1993–2018) before joining Toyo University (~2018).

Masako Keta specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1981) and later served there as Professor of Philosophy of Religion (~2000–2018) following posts at Aichi University of Technology Automotive Junior College and Kanazawa University.

Masamichi Ichigo studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani University, Kyoto University, and the University of Michigan under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao. He held professorships at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (2006–2010) under the supervision of Helmut Krasser.

Masamichi Yamada studied Buddhist studies under traditional teacher Koun Yamada and attended Harvard Business School. His career includes posts at Mitsubishi Bank (~1964–1996), Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Mitsubishi UFJ Securities, Tokyu Railways, and Itoki Corporation (~2004–2016).
Masanori Shono is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who has held an assistant professorship at Osaka University and a researcher post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University and Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, Keiji Nishitani, and D. T. Suzuki, later holding posts at Kyoto University and Nara University of Education.
Masao Shizutani worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He held assistant professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Masao Yamaguchi studied at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo Metropolitan University, working in Japanology and religious studies. He held academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1967–1994), University of Shizuoka (~1994–1999), and Sapporo University (~1999–2003).
Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1965–1974) and later served there as an assistant professor (~1982–2017).

Masato Kobayashi specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and earned his Ph.D. under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000), later serving as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2001).
Masatoshi Konishi was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1963) and held an academic post at Rikkyo University (~1974–2004).

Masatoshi Nagatomi specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1951) and Harvard University (~1953–1957), where he subsequently served as a professor from ~1958 to 1996.

Masayuki Taira works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. After studying at Kyoto University (~1970–1979), he held academic posts at Kansai University (~1990–1995), Osaka University (~1995–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2017–2022).

Mathieu Boisvert specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at the Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992 and founded the GRIMER research group.
